body:
`rcf` goals with irrational coefficients spend most of their kernel time proving the signs of individual field elements, one full Sturm certificate per element. Replace this with interval evaluation against the generator's isolating interval, which the certificate already contains.

For `example : ∃ x : ℝ, x ^ 2 = Real.sqrt 2 ∧ 1 < x ∧ x < 2 := by rcf` the problem is a degree-4 polynomial over ℚ(√2), about the size of a degree-8 rational problem, which the rational path decides in under a second. This goal takes about 14 s of kernel time instead. Measured with `set_option diagnostics true` on chungus2 under load, so absolute times vary up to 2x but the proportions were stable:

- about 30% goes to the literal sign table: about 96 entries, each proving the sign of one element `a + b√2` with its own rational Sturm certificate, re-proving the same chain for `X² − 2` on the same interval every time;
- about 45% goes to 12 root-sign certificates with coefficients in ℚ(√2), whose sign lookups go through that table;
- every lookup is a linear `List.find?` over the table with structural comparison of keys made of `Rat` lists, about 31k `PolyQuot` equality tests and 31k `List.find?` steps in this goal.

The replay is `quoteCertificate` in `adapters/HexRCF/RealCoefficients/FieldLiteral.lean` (around lines 264 to 316), which splits the check with `simp only` and runs `decide +kernel` on each piece.

To fix:

- Decide the sign of a field element `a(θ)` by evaluating `a` over the certified isolating interval of `θ` in exact rational arithmetic, refining the interval only when the result is inconclusive. For a quadratic field, comparing `a²` with `d·b²` is exact and needs no refinement.
- Look signs up by index, not by linear search over structurally compared keys.

The estimated gain is 2 to 4x on these goals. The manual's examples `∃ x, x² = √2 ∧ 1 < x ∧ x < 2`, `∃ x, x² = 1 / (√2 + 1) ∧ 0 < x ∧ x < 1` and the `2 ^ (1 / 3)` examples in `HexManual/Chapters/HexRCF.lean` are suitable benchmarks.

🤖 Prepared with Claude Code

comments.body:
This is incorporated into the continuing #10358 work. The current merged fixed-field path uses exact interval/Horner sign evidence, checked indexed sign-table routing, and checked contained count-one generator-window transport. The window tranche landed in [#10692](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/pull/10692), squash `73b6a0ecfa41d3586a4327d974e0e5920c314aab` (green required CI). Exact artifacts include `LiteralSign.lean` (`Window`), `FieldRefinement.lean`, `FieldLiteral.lean`, `SignIndex.lean` and `conformance/HexRCF/GeneratorWindow.lean`. Every route retains the original selected root/embedding and exact keys. Frozen replay performs no refinement, sign/root search or fallback after false/exhausted/invalid evidence.

The retained [index comparison](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/blob/main/reports/hexrcf-index-proofs.md) favors checked indexed retrieval in all adjacent pairs of its two source-distinct 24-arm studies. The [window comparison](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/blob/main/reports/hexrcf-window-proofs.md) and separate precision studies retain all completed samples and establish no reliable whole-module refinement speedup; refinement therefore defaults to zero. The original estimated 2–4× gain is not claimed as a measured general result. The [evidence inventory](https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev/blob/main/reports/hexrcf-adapter-evidence.md) states the exact measured sources and limitations. #10358 remains open for its full backend/API/manual scope; no new decomposition issue or worker has been launched.

title: perf(rcf): decide field-element signs by interval evaluation, not one Sturm certificate each
